text:
Chicago arrives in Sunrise on a slide: winless in three (0-2-1) and coming off a 5-2 home loss to Colorado, a game the Avalanche won after trailing by two. The Blackhawks are without Bowen Byram and Patrick Kane, and Teuvo Teravainen has moved onto the first power-play unit. Florida lost 5-3 to Detroit on Monday, ending a three-game winning streak, and still lacks Brad Marchand and Aleksander Barkov. Sam Bennett has stepped in beside Sam Reinhart and Brady Tkachuk, and Lars Eller, who plays his 1,200th NHL game, is up to 17:11 a night.

The teams met on Oct. 25, when Florida won 3-2. Over the season, Florida has controlled the chances at five on five, with 54% of the expected goals (a measure of shot quality) to Chicago's 40%. Florida's power play (1.12 expected goals a game) also outclasses Chicago's (0.55), though the Panthers take 5.4 penalties a game. In net, Chicago projects Spencer Knight (+2.4 goals saved above expected this season, +11.1 last year) against Jacob Markstrom (+0.2 now, -16.0 last year). Our model has Florida scoring 3.5 goals to Chicago's 2.9.

Connor Bedard is 36% to score for Chicago, with a six-game point streak. Reinhart (40% to score) and Seth Jones, who has 17 points in 10 games, lead Florida. Our under-the-radar picks: Bennett, whose shots have been dangerous for a third-liner (26% to score), and Roman Kantserov, 52% for a point because his line creates chances. Projected goalies may change.
